answers.question: Q9
answers.correction: These parts hold. No school text gives a potential, an order parameter or Goldstone modes for the choice of polarization. FLM call GR's breaking kinematical and propose a dynamical splitting. 'Vacuum selection' means the string-vacuum problem. The other choice is equally lawful. 2104.00802 (v1 2021-04-01; the passage is in the v1 PDF, pp. 5–6) puts a breaking tied to the choice of polarization 'at the level of the vacuum sector', and no record file quotes it. Corrections: (1) 'The symmetry is restored as one goes back in time' concerns the Lorentz symmetry violated by the infrared dispersion relation (17) in the cosmological frame, not the dual Lorentz symmetry. The essay calls the dual symmetry 'fundamentally broken at the quantum level'. (2) The essay gives its own reason for that breaking: 'the dual Lorentz action is not a canonical transformation' (eq. 12). It does not preserve [x̂, x̂̃] = iπλ², so it is not a symmetry of the essay's quantum theory. The program's ρ and its U(1) preserve ω (P2′, P3). So 2104.00802 anticipates the phrase 'symmetry breaking ... at the level of the vacuum sector', said of a non-canonical symmetry of a doubled (x, x̃) space, together with 'a choice of ground state' and the expansion as selector. It does not anticipate the program's structure, an exact ω-preserving symmetry broken by the vacuum. The reader's test of #11 §3 ('does not hold for the vacuum as the place where the breaking occurs') is too strong. (3) 'None calls that choice spontaneous', and the test's 'holds for the word spontaneous', need qualifying. Berglund, Hübsch and Minic 2022 (2212.06086 §4.3, citing 2104.00802 as [250]) call O(1,d−1)₂ 'effectively spontaneously broken' within the sector of fixed nonzero p̃. That is the same dual Lorentz group, whose orbits δ labels. It is the symmetry tied to the polarization, though not ρ, and it comes with no order parameter or potential. (4) Missed: 1606.01829 §2 (2016; also J. Phys. Conf. Ser. 804 012032 §6) names the coset over which the program's order parameter ranges: 'The space U(d)/O(d) represents the choice of inequivalent lifts η that preserve the symplectic structure and the vacuum state'. It is named as a space of choices, with no potential. The same section argues that choosing a modular polarization does not break a canonical symmetry, since 'any other modular space is related to the original one by a change of polarization, i.e., a canonical transformation'. (5) 'The one school text' that places the breaking in the vacuum: add 2212.06086 §4.3 as its restatement in 'spontaneous' terms.

Minic 2020 §5, read by the reader, says dark quanta 'should be detectable through their particular metaparticle entanglement to visible matter'. It ties them to modified dark matter, whose critical acceleration '∼cH' ('of the order of 10^{-10}m/s^{2}', the paper's figure) 'is found in correlations between dark matter and baryonic matter in galaxy rotation curves'. record_contradictions.record_says: #11 §3: 'They treat the breaking as kinematical and call the choice "a dynamical question".' wiki/phase-space/reciprocity/broken-born-duality.md: 'treated the breaking as kinematical, not as spontaneous symmetry breaking'. notes/toy-lagrangian.md, Chunk 1 results: 'call Born's breaking kinematical, not spontaneous.'
record_contradictions.note: The sources are as quoted (1405.3949 §1.1, §1.3, §2; 1502.08005 §2.1 p. 11; all FOUND). 'Kinematical' is FLM's word for GR's breaking, and their proposal makes the splitting dynamical. So the wiki's 'treated the breaking as kinematical', beside its own 'made η dynamical', misdescribes the proposal. Against #11 §3 the item is weaker than the reader says. (i) The same sentence reports the dynamical side, accurately ('a dynamical question', p. 47). (ii) The selector [26S] itself exhibits is a consistency condition: worldsheet locality selects L-projectability (§6.1 p. 39; §7 p. 47). The reader's own reading of that passage calls it 'a kinematical selection, as #11 §3 says'. (iii) 'Kinematical breaking' is 1405.3949's phrase; [26S] uses 'kinematical' only for η in GR. (iv) §3 and P2′ do not conflict: one reports FLM's view of the breaking, the other credits [26S] with a dynamical η. The worklog's sentence is scoped to 1307.7080 and 1405.3949 and is accurate for them.

record_contradictions.record_says: #11 §3: 'This program's addition is to read it as spontaneous breaking, with η as the order parameter'. Wiki description: 'they gave no potential and no symmetry-breaking analysis'. Worklog: 'They write no potential and do no symmetry-breaking analysis'.
record_contradictions.note: Confirmed: 2104.00802 (v1 2021-04-01, v1 PDF pp. 5–6) ties a symmetry breaking to the choice of polarization and places it 'at the level of the vacuum sector'. No record file quotes it: a repository grep for 'vacuum sector', 'decoupling frame' and 'choice of ground state' gives 0 hits, and the literature check cites the essay only for C1. Corrections: (1) 'the symmetry is restored as one goes back in time' is the Lorentz symmetry of dispersion relation (17), not the dual symmetry. (2) The essay's reason for the breaking is 'In other words the dual Lorentz action is not a canonical transformation': the broken symmetry does not preserve the commutator, whereas #11's ρ preserves ω. Two paragraphs with no vacua compared and no potential are a statement, not a symmetry-breaking analysis. So 'no symmetry-breaking analysis' survives narrowly; 'nothing on a breaking tied to the polarization' would not. (3) 'The word spontaneous is absent' holds for 2104.00802 only. 2212.06086 §4.3 (2022, citing 2104.00802 as [250]) calls the same group O(1,d−1)₂ 'effectively spontaneously broken'. So the program's own addition is narrower than the reader's list: an exact ω-preserving symmetry (ρ inside its U(1)) broken by the vacuum, η as order parameter, the potential, the Goldstone angle and the K-sign lock. The bare word 'spontaneous' has a school precedent. The coset U(d)/O(d) of η-choices at fixed ω and vacuum is named, as a space of choices, in 1606.01829 §2. (4) The worklog's sentence is scoped to 1307.7080 and 1405.3949 and stays accurate. What 2104.00802 and 2212.06086 contradict is the wiki's generalization to FLM's metastring work.

record_contradictions.record_says: notes/literature-check.md §3, 'The vacuum': 'The check found no such mechanism in the school's papers, where the classical spacetime label "corresponds to a choice" of polarization.' §2 plain-language passage: 'a vacuum that selects a polarization, and a dark sector coupled to ours by gravity alone'.
record_contradictions.note: §3's 'such mechanism' points back to 'the spontaneous reading, with η as the order parameter'. Neither 2104.00802 nor 2212.06086 has that, so §3 stands as written. The §2 sentence does need narrowing. 2104.00802 joins a vacuum-level fixing of the spacetime frame to a hedged dark-sector speculation ('seems to have potential for an entirely novel source for dark matter/energy, with states of class II being remnants'). But the reader overstates when it says 'a vacuum that selects a polarization' joined to a dual dark sector is published. In the essay the ground state is chosen ('a choice of ground state fixes a value of δ'). The selector it proposes is the expansion, an outside input. The broken symmetry is non-canonical, in a doubled (x, x̃) space at λ² = ℏα′. The candidates are 'dark matter/energy', undecided. The reader is right that 'corresponds to a choice' ends 'with a contextuality parameter λ' (2407.06207 §3.3).

Flag 64's 'selected spontaneously' needs narrowing too, since 2212.06086 §4.3 calls the dual Lorentz group, the one 2104.00802 ties to the polarization, 'effectively spontaneously broken'. Three differences survive the sources read here. The broken symmetry is a canonical, ω-preserving ρ, against a non-canonical dual Lorentz group. η is an order parameter with a potential and a Goldstone angle; the school has neither. One vacuum holds for all matter. On scope, 2104.00802's own selection is universal ('the expansion of the Universe gives rise to a preferred frame'). The observer- and context-dependent readings the reader cites (804 012032 §6, 2407.06207 §3.5, 2503.20854 §1) are the school's other line.

Each candidate in the literature either selects the pair only, or uses outside input...'. Wiki: 'the worklog finds that a mechanism picking one section over its partner is open in the literature'.
record_contradictions.note: Confirmed: the worklog does not cite 2104.00802 (repository grep), and its 'Claimed only in words' list omits FKLM 2021, which works a simple model (eqs. 13–17: dual-momentum states decouple as a_c → ∞). Not confirmed: the charge that the wiki overstates. FKLM's mechanism falls in the worklog's own class 'uses outside input: which modes are light', so the worklog's 'Open' stands as written. The wiki's paraphrase matches the worklog, whose S5 conclusion says of the strong form 'It is also open in the literature'. The wiki drops information, that outside-input candidates exist; it does not overstate.

That is the coset over which #11 P2′'s order parameter ranges at fixed ω and H. The toy-model worklog's compact Goldstone is 'the Lagrangian Grassmannian Λ(1)', and flag 61 uses Λ(4). missed.quote: So indeed the rotation maps one modular space T_{\Lambda} into another T_{\mathbb{O}\Lambda} , but since by construction, a modular space is a choice of polarization, any other modular space is related to the original one by a change of polarization, i.e., a canonical transformation.
missed.why_it_matters: This is the school's own analysis of a symmetry acting on the choice of polarization. The lattice 'naively breaks rotational invariance', but 'this is not the right conclusion if space is modular' (same section). With 2104.00802's 'not a canonical transformation', the school's line is that a canonical change of polarization is not broken by choosing one, and that the symmetry it calls broken is non-canonical. #11 reads the canonical ρ as spontaneously broken by the vacuum (§3, P5).

In §2.8, p. 19 (PDF p. 30), a speculation: 'The observation that the Schrödinger and momentum representations require different gauge fixings might be useful for developing quantum theories that break the Born reciprocity. If the modular U(1) gauge symmetry is somehow broken, this may be used as a mechanism to fix the quantum configuration space.' Of a cosmological-scale modular length it says 'This would break the Born reciprocity in favor of the position variables spanning the configuration space', and it adds that the scenario 'is not possible in the simple system we discuss here because of the Stone-von Neumann theorem'. It also calls η 'the geometric construct that singles out the position and momentum spaces'. These passages are not code-checkable: they are thesis-only, absent from its arXiv source 2002.01604 (lit.py quote: NOT FOUND). The thesis is later than 2104.00802 and earlier than the program.

overall: The reader's quotations, dates, pages and sections can be relied on. All 133 quotations were found, 128 by lit.py and 5 in the IOP PDF of 804 012032. Its central find also holds: 2104.00802, in v1 of 2021-04-01, ties a dual-Lorentz breaking to the choice of polarization 'at the level of the vacuum sector', and the record never quotes it. Its interpretation of that find overreaches and must be corrected before use. The symmetry 'restored as one goes back in time' is Lorentz symmetry. The broken symmetry 'is not a canonical transformation', so this is not an exact ω-preserving symmetry broken by a vacuum. 2212.06086 calls the same group 'effectively spontaneously broken'. 1606.01829 §2 names U(d)/O(d) as the space of η-choices. Outside Q9 it misplaces Minic 2020's dark sector on x̃ and wrongly answers Q5 as not addressed.
